note: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (spec §13). Every gate and the site itself read this file.
Pixel positions are NOT stored — they are derived from `constants` by milestoneY() in src/lib/timeline.ts,
so a date cannot be verified in one place and shipped from another.
Genus names are marked with *asterisks* and rendered as <em>; the plain-text form is what a screen reader gets.
Sections still to be filled by their own build steps: field keyframes (§6), solved scrims (solve-scrim.ts),

arrivals.name: The Solar System forms
arrivals.line: Dust and ice collapse around a new star. Nothing older has ever been dated.
arrivals.analogy: a fist-sized slice of stony meteorite, cut and polished flat: a dark grey matrix studded with a scatter of pale chalky-white, irregular rounded blobs a centimetre or two across
arrivals.negative: not a planet, not a swirling disc of dust and gas, not a starfield — one physical rock, cut open and held still, the oldest dated solid material in the solar system rather than an artist's impression of its birth. The matrix stays a mid-to-dark grey, never black or near-black, or the luminance key punches holes through it; the pale inclusions are chalky white-grey, dull, not glowing and not metallic.
arrivals.reference: Allende meteorite CAI specimen photographs — AMNH 4880 (amnh.org); Connelly et al. 2012, *Science*

arrivals.name: Earth reaches full size
arrivals.line: Accretion finishes. The whole surface is molten rock.
arrivals.analogy: a ball of liquid rock, glowing orange-red, brighter yellow-white cracks, a few darker cooling crusts floating on it
arrivals.negative: not a rocky planet with lava rivers

arrivals.name: The Moon is torn out
arrivals.line: A Mars-sized body strikes, at least 4.51 billion years ago. The debris becomes a Moon that hangs enormous and close.
arrivals.analogy: a small sphere of molten rock hanging alone against black, dull orange-red overall with brighter cracks of yellow-white light breaking through its surface
arrivals.negative: not the grey, cratered Moon of today — freshly torn from Earth it is still glowing rock, the same register as the Earth-full-size portrait rather than a rocky moon. Nothing on it may be black or near-black; darker patches read as dimmer glow, never as dark holes or shadow.
arrivals.reference: giant-impact hypothesis reconstructions (NASA/SwRI simulation renders); styled to match the molten-Hadean Earth portrait already baked, §11

arrivals.line: The Moon is two and a half times wider than it is today

arrivals.name: Liquid water
arrivals.line: A single zircon crystal records water at the surface.
arrivals.analogy: one tiny gem-like crystal shown much larger than life, reddish-brown and translucent, a slender six-sided prism with pointed pyramidal ends, alone against black
arrivals.negative: not a boulder, not a cluster, not a vein in rock — a single isolated crystal, magnified the way a specimen diagram magnifies something smaller than a grain of rice. Reddish-brown to amber and translucent, never black or near-black, and never cut with flat gemstone facets — natural crystal faces only.
arrivals.reference: Jack Hills zircon grain photomicrographs — Cavosie et al. 2018 review figures; Wilde et al. 2001, *Nature*

arrivals.name: Steam and acid rain
arrivals.line: The air is CO₂. The rain is acid. There is nothing yet you would call land.
arrivals.analogy: a single pitted, etched volcanic rock in mid-toned warm grey and rust, its pits shown as shallow dents a shade or two darker than the surface, with pale streaks of rain running down its face
arrivals.negative: not a landscape or a storm scene — one rock specimen and nothing else in its quarter of the picture, no loose fragments or stray marks floating near it. Nothing anywhere on the rock may be black or near-black: the pits are mid-grey dents, not dark holes, and the rock overall is a light-to-mid value. The rain is drawn as pale streaks ON the rock's face, running down it. Two rounds (2026-07-31): the first was near-black and the key punched every pit out of the artwork; the second keyed correctly but lost the rain and left a stray orange fragment floating above the rock.

arrivals.name: The oldest surviving crust
arrivals.line: Nuvvuagittuq, Quebec — a scrap of the first ocean floor.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of grey-beige banded rock, its bands running in soft parallel waves, with a scatter of small dark purple-red garnet flecks caught in the pale bands
arrivals.negative: not dark green like an ordinary amphibolite — this rock's whole identity is that it is paler than the rock it resembles ('faux'-amphibolite). The base colour is light grey-beige, never black or near-black, and the banding is soft and wavy, not tightly folded like the Rodinia gneiss elsewhere on this page.
arrivals.reference: Nuvvuagittuq faux-amphibolite specimen photographs — sciencemall-usa.com; Flickr (jsjgeology); O'Neil et al. 2025, *Science*

arrivals.name: The oldest rock we still have
arrivals.line: Acasta gneiss, north-west Canada. The Hadean ends here because this is where the record starts.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of streaky rock, straight alternating bands of pale pinkish-grey and darker brownish-grey, with a few small red garnet flecks
arrivals.negative: not tightly folded like the later Rodinia gneiss elsewhere on this page — these bands run straighter and more evenly striped. The darker bands stay a mid brownish-grey, never black or near-black.
arrivals.reference: Acasta Gneiss specimen photographs — Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre; C&EN 2023 (cen.acs.org)

arrivals.name: The oldest sedimentary rocks
arrivals.line: Isua, Greenland — mud, laid down under water, by a real ocean.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of fine-grained rock split along its bedding, showing dozens of thin, slightly wavy parallel layers stacked like the pages of a closed book, pale grey-green throughout
arrivals.negative: not the bold red-and-black striping of a banded iron formation — that is a different, later rock on this page. These layers are finer, closer together and all in a narrow grey-green range: the record of ordinary mud settling in water, not iron precipitating out of it. Nothing in the layers may be black or near-black.
arrivals.reference: Isua supracrustal belt metasediment specimen photographs — FossilEra; Nutman et al. 1997, *Precambrian Res.*

arrivals.name: The first trace of life
arrivals.line: Isotopically light carbon in Isua sediment. Not a fossil — a chemical shadow, and the oldest one anyone accepts.
arrivals.analogy: the same pale grey-green layered rock as the Isua sediment beside it on this page, but with a scatter of dull dark-grey graphite specks and short streaks caught between its layers, like flecks of pencil lead in stone
arrivals.negative: not a fossil and not any visible shape of a living thing — the evidence is chemical, a carbon isotope ratio, not a body, so nothing organism-shaped may appear anywhere on the rock. The graphite specks are dull dark grey, never black or near-black, or the luminance key punches them out of the artwork. First round (2026-08-01): the rock itself matched, but it shared a sheet with Tiktaalik in the adjacent quadrant, whose snout sat hard against the sheet's vertical midline and bled a sliver of orange across it — inflating this quadrant's trimmed bounding box to 779×623 against its sibling rock's 600×501. Not a fault of this subject's own prompt; redo needs its neighbour drawn with real clearance from the boundary, not a change to this description.
arrivals.reference: Isua metasediment graphite-inclusion specimen photographs (same locality as the oldest sedimentary rocks); Rosing 1999, *Science*; Ohtomo et al. 2014

arrivals.name: Microbial mats
arrivals.line: Life is a film on the seabed, and stays that way for three billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a broad, low, wrinkled sheet lying flat on sediment, like the crumpled skin on cooled paint — olive-green and brown, puckered into ridges and shallow domes a few centimetres across
arrivals.negative: not coral, not seaweed, not any branching or upright growth: a microbial mat is a flat film ON the sediment, with no stems, fronds or plant-like structure. Not a stromatolite either — no built-up column and no internal layering, those arrive later on this page. Keep it light-to-mid in value; the shadows between wrinkles are shallow dents, never near-black.
arrivals.reference: modern Shark Bay and Sippewissett microbial mat photographs; Noffke et al. 2013, *Astrobiology*

arrivals.name: Stromatolites
arrivals.line: Mats build the first structures life leaves behind. Whether these particular ones did is still argued.
arrivals.analogy: a rounded, layered mound of banded rock, like a stack of thin stone plates or a cross-section of a cabbage
arrivals.negative: not a mushroom, not a shell, not a visible living creature — a banded rock structure
arrivals.source: Dresser Fm. 3.48 Ga; Baumgartner et al. 2024

arrivals.name: Microbes that eat sulfur
arrivals.line: No oxygen, no sunlight needed — chemistry alone.
arrivals.analogy: a cluster of tiny rod- and sphere-shaped cells at high magnification, translucent pale yellow-green, each scattered with bright sulfur granules inside it like mustard seeds suspended in glass
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not an animal, not anything with a body plan — these are single cells. Not chlorophyll-green leafy algae: the colour comes from sulfur, so it reads pale yellow and warm. No cell may be near-black, and the granules must stay bright.
arrivals.reference: Wacey et al. 2011, *Nature Geoscience* — Strelley Pool microfossils; modern sulfur-oxidising bacteria light micrographs

arrivals.name: A fifty-kilometre asteroid
arrivals.line: The S2 impact — 50 to 200 times the mass of the one that killed the dinosaurs. It boils the top of the ocean, and life gets better.
arrivals.analogy: one irregular potato-shaped rock tumbling alone, pitted all over with shallow overlapping craters like Phobos, in warm mid-grey and tan
arrivals.negative: not a fireball, not a streaking meteor with a flame trail, and not an impact scene with Earth in frame — this is the body itself, a single cratered rock. Craters are shallow dents a shade or two darker, never black holes, or the luminance key punches them out of the artwork.
arrivals.reference: Phobos and Bennu spacecraft imagery; Drabon et al. 2024, *PNAS* — S2 impactor, 37–58 km

arrivals.name: The first continents
arrivals.line: Cratons stabilise. There is now permanent dry land.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized block of coarse pink-and-grey granite, speckled with large blocky feldspar crystals, glassy quartz and small flecks of mica — the light, buoyant rock continents are made of
arrivals.negative: not the fine dark banding of a gneiss: the oldest rock elsewhere on this page is a gneiss and these two must not read as the same specimen. Granite is coarse and speckled, never layered. Not a landscape, not an island, not a map — one hand specimen. Mica flecks are mid-grey, never black.
arrivals.reference: coarse-grained granite hand-specimen photographs; Hawkesworth et al. 2020

arrivals.name: Photosynthesis
arrivals.line: Cyanobacteria split water and let the oxygen go. It will take 600 million years to matter.
arrivals.source: Sánchez-Baracaldo et al. 2021, *Proc. R. Soc. B*
arrivals.analogy: a single gently curved filament of blue-green cells strung end to end like a string of beads inside a clear sheath, each cell a rounded cylinder
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf, not seaweed — a cyanobacterium is one filament of cells. Not grass-green: the colour is a distinctive blue-green. The sheath is translucent, not a dark outline, and no cell may be near-black.
arrivals.reference: modern *Oscillatoria* and *Nostoc* light micrographs; Sánchez-Baracaldo et al. 2021, *Proc. R. Soc. B*

arrivals.name: The first ice age
arrivals.line: The Pongola glaciation. Ice at mid-latitudes, on a planet with no oxygen.
arrivals.source: Young et al. 1998; Ojakangas et al. 2014
arrivals.analogy: a rounded boulder of pale grey diamictite — angular pebbles of many sizes frozen into a fine matrix, like fruitcake turned to stone — with one flat face bearing straight parallel scratches where ice dragged it across bedrock
arrivals.negative: not a snowy landscape, not a glacier and not an iceberg: the evidence for the first ice age is a rock. Not a smooth beach cobble — the embedded clasts must be angular and unsorted. The scratches are shallow grooves, never black lines.
arrivals.reference: glacial diamictite and striated pavement specimen photographs; Young et al. 1998; Ojakangas et al. 2014

arrivals.name: Cyanobacteria, everywhere
arrivals.line: Still no free oxygen in the air — the rock is drinking all of it.
arrivals.analogy: a dense tangle of many blue-green filaments massed together into a loose floating mat, each filament a chain of rounded cells like a string of beads
arrivals.negative: the same organism as the photosynthesis subject earlier on this page, drawn as a crowd rather than one strand, and it must read as the same material. Not a plant, not seaweed, not leafy, not branching. No dark outlines and nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: as photosynthesis — modern *Oscillatoria* and *Nostoc* light micrographs

arrivals.name: Whiffs of oxygen
arrivals.line: Oxygen appears in patches, hundreds of millions of years before the air changes.
arrivals.analogy: a cluster of small bubbles rising off a mat of green scum, like carbonation
arrivals.negative: not fire or an explosion — gas bubbles, not flame

arrivals.line: The sky flickers orange and back, three to five times
arrivals.source: Zerkle et al. 2012; Izon et al. 2015, 2017

arrivals.name: Banded iron
arrivals.line: Oxygen meets dissolved iron and it rusts out of the sea, in bands, for a billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a cut block of banded iron formation standing on end, crossed by dozens of narrow wavy parallel bands — deep brick-red and maroon jasper alternating with silver-grey iron layers, the bands gently folded, varying in thickness, some pinching out and some swelling
arrivals.negative: not a cliff, canyon or landscape, and not an abstract stripe pattern: one hand-sized specimen with rough broken edges. Not the fine even grey-green layering of the Isua sediment elsewhere on this page — these bands are bold, red and high-contrast. The silver-grey bands are a mid-tone metallic grey, never black.
arrivals.reference: banded iron formation hand-specimen photographs (Hamersley, Marquette); Bekker et al. 2010, *Econ. Geol.*

arrivals.name: Banded iron, still
arrivals.line: Still rusting out of the sea. It has been a hundred million years.
arrivals.analogy: the same banded iron formation as earlier on this page, drawn as a broader, thicker slab — many more red-and-silver bands stacked across it, the layering denser and the folding tighter
arrivals.negative: the same rock as the 2,600 Ma banded iron and it must read as the same material: bold red jasper alternating with metallic silver-grey. Not a landscape and not a stripe pattern. The silver bands stay mid-tone grey, never black.
arrivals.reference: as banded-iron — Bekker et al. 2010, *Econ. Geol.*

arrivals.name: The Great Oxidation begins
arrivals.line: Free oxygen floods the air and poisons most of the life that made it.
arrivals.analogy: smooth and featureless like Titan, thick orange-tan haze, faint soft banding, no continents or oceans visible
arrivals.negative: not Jupiter — no bold stripes, no storms

arrivals.name: The Huronian glaciation
arrivals.line: Oxygen destroys the methane greenhouse and the planet freezes, three times over.
arrivals.analogy: a single buff boulder dropped into fine layered mud, the layers directly beneath it bent and sagging under its weight — a dropstone, the signature of ice rafting
arrivals.negative: not a snowy scene, not a glacier and not an iceberg: the evidence is a rock. The bending of the layers underneath is the whole point and must be clearly visible. Not the striated boulder used for the first ice age earlier on this page — this one sits in sediment. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Gowganda Formation dropstone photographs; Young 2013

arrivals.line: The sky is blue

arrivals.name: The Great Oxidation ends
arrivals.line: Oxygen is permanent. The haze never comes back.
arrivals.analogy: a rust-red rock slab seen close, with a crack of open blue sky at the top
arrivals.negative: not a full landscape — one slab, the sky a sliver behind it

arrivals.name: Francevillian structures?
arrivals.line: Centimetre-scale shapes in Gabon. Possibly the oldest multicellular life; possibly not life at all.
arrivals.analogy: several flat, lobed, coin-sized discs on a slab of buff mudstone, each with a crinkled raised rim and a smoother middle, like blobs of dried wax pressed into the rock
arrivals.negative: not a fossil animal, not a shell, and nothing with recognisable body parts — whether these are life at all is disputed, so they must read as ambiguous shapes in rock rather than as a creature. Not regular circles like coins: the outlines are irregular and lobed. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: El Albani et al. 2010, *Nature*; El Albani et al. 2014, *PLoS ONE* — Francevillian B specimens

arrivals.line: Oxygen falls back

arrivals.name: *Grypania*?
arrivals.line: A coiled ribbon in Michigan iron. Big enough to see, but nothing of its cells survives.
arrivals.analogy: a single flat ribbon coiled into a loose open spiral on a reddish slab of iron-rich rock, like a length of tape laid down in a curl — smooth-edged, uniform in width, about a centimetre across
arrivals.negative: not a shell and not an ammonite: no chambers, no ribs, no ridges. It is a smooth featureless ribbon, and nothing of its internal structure survives. Not a worm with a head or segments. The carbon film reads mid-grey against the red rock, never near-black, or the luminance key punches it out.
arrivals.reference: Han & Runnegar 1992, *Science* — *Grypania spiralis*, Negaunee Iron Formation

arrivals.line: Banded iron stops
arrivals.source: Bekker et al. 2010 — end of major BIF

arrivals.name: The first complex cells
arrivals.line: *Qingshania* — cells with a nucleus, stuck together on purpose.
arrivals.analogy: a short straight filament of a few large box-shaped cells joined end to end like the carriages of a train, each cell far chunkier than a bacterium and holding one softly-defined rounded body inside it
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf and not seaweed. Not a thin bacterial thread — the whole point is that these cells are large and compartmented, each carrying a nucleus, so they must look chunky and blocky rather than hair-like. The nucleus is a soft mid-toned disc, never a black dot.
arrivals.reference: Miao et al. 2024, *Sci. Adv.* — *Qingshania magnifica*

arrivals.name: Sex
arrivals.line: *Bangiomorpha*, a red alga. The oldest known sexual reproduction.
arrivals.analogy: a short upright tuft of red alga: a single unbranched filament of stacked disc-shaped cells, like a narrow pile of coins, anchored at its base by a small holdfast
arrivals.negative: not a leafy frond, not kelp and not a branching plant — *Bangiomorpha* is one narrow filament of stacked cells on a holdfast. Not green: it is a red alga, so a warm pink-red. No dark outline and nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Gibson et al. 2018, *Geology*; modern *Bangia* micrographs — *Bangiomorpha pubescens*

arrivals.name: Rodinia
arrivals.line: Every continent, gathered into one mass.
arrivals.analogy: a specimen of folded gneiss — a banded rock whose pink, grey and pale mineral stripes are bent into tight parallel folds, as if the layers had been squeezed from both sides
arrivals.negative: not a map, not a landmass, not a continent and not a globe — one rock specimen seen close. The bands are smooth continuous folded stripes, not cracks and not loose brushstrokes. Nothing anywhere on it may be black or near-black. Two rounds (2026-07-31) drew the modern African continent, with Madagascar, when this milestone was prompted as a landmass silhouette — a negative naming Africa did not stop it. The subject is therefore the rock that continental collision makes (the Grenville orogeny, ~1.1–0.9 Ga, is Rodinia's assembly) rather than the shape of the supercontinent.

arrivals.name: The first sponges?
arrivals.line: Sponge-like structures in Canadian reef rock, 300 million years before any agreed animal.
arrivals.analogy: an irregular pale lump of reef limestone with a fine network of branching tubes winding through it, like a tangle of thread or the vermicular texture inside a bath sponge, exposed on a cut face
arrivals.negative: not a modern vase- or barrel-shaped sponge sitting on a reef: what survives is a microscopic meshwork inside rock, and the identification is disputed, so this is a rock specimen with a tube network in it rather than an animal. The tubes are mid-toned, never near-black holes.
arrivals.reference: Turner 2021, *Nature* — Little Dal reef vermiform microstructure

arrivals.line: The Boring Billion ends

arrivals.name: Snowball Earth
arrivals.line: Ice reaches the tropics. The Sturtian lasts 56 million years.
arrivals.analogy: ice pole to pole, pale blue-grey fracture lines like cracked porcelain, a few small bare rock patches near the middle
arrivals.negative: not a modern Earth with white poles and blue oceans

arrivals.name: The ice retreats
arrivals.line: Cap carbonate, laid down in a few thousand years on top of the ice.
arrivals.analogy: a slab of pale cream-and-buff limestone in fine even layers, its top surface crossed by low rolling ripples, sitting sharply on a rougher darker rock beneath — the boundary between the two flat and abrupt
arrivals.negative: not an iceberg, not a glacier and not melting ice: the evidence is the rock that formed on top of what the ice left. Not the red-and-silver banding of banded iron — cap carbonate is pale, creamy and finely layered. The rock beneath stays mid-toned, never black.
arrivals.reference: Marinoan and Sturtian cap carbonate outcrop and hand-specimen photographs; Rooney et al. 2015, *Geology*

arrivals.name: The ice breaks for good
arrivals.line: A second freeze, the Marinoan — perhaps only four million years — and then it is over. The Ediacaran begins.
arrivals.source: ICS base Ediacaran 635.0 Ma; Wang et al. 2025, *PNAS*
arrivals.analogy: a rounded slab of glacial diamictite whose top half gives way to smooth even meltwater-laid bedding — jumbled angular pebbles below, quiet flat layers above, with a clean line between them
arrivals.negative: not a landscape, not an ice sheet and not a thaw scene: one rock specimen recording the transition. It must read as the same family of glacial rock as the earlier ice subjects on this page. Nothing near-black between the clasts.
arrivals.reference: Marinoan diamictite–cap carbonate contact specimens; ICS base Ediacaran 635.0 Ma; Wang et al. 2025, *PNAS*

arrivals.name: *Charnia*
arrivals.line: The first big bodies — soft, strange, rooted to the seabed.
arrivals.analogy: a frond like a fern or chestnut leaf, branching ridges repeating as smaller copies of themselves down its length, rooted to the seabed by a small disc
arrivals.negative: not a plant or seaweed — no leaves branching off a stem, one long frond of self-similar ridges

arrivals.name: The Cambrian begins
arrivals.line: Shells, eyes, guts, predators, and the first things burrowing through mud on purpose.
arrivals.analogy: a trilobite seen from directly above: a flat oval shield divided lengthwise into three lobes, a broad crescent head bearing two crescent eyes, a jointed thorax of repeated segments, and a small tail plate
arrivals.negative: not a woodlouse, not a horseshoe crab and not a beetle — the three lengthwise lobes and the crescent head shield are the defining shapes and must be unmistakable. No insect antennae. Keep it a warm mid-toned brown-orange, never near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Olenellus* and *Paradoxides* specimen photographs; ICS 2023 — 538.8 ± 0.6 Ma

arrivals.name: The Burgess Shale
arrivals.line: *Anomalocaris* — a metre of segmented predator, with the first real eyes.
arrivals.analogy: a flattened, segmented swimmer with rows of side fins like a shrimp, two large stalked eyes, two long spiny grasping arms held out in front like a pair of curved combs, and underneath the head a small circular ring of overlapping plates, like a camera aperture, as its mouth
arrivals.negative: no pincers, no crab or lobster claws, no snapping jaws of any kind — the front arms are segmented and spiny like a centipede's legs held forward, not a claw that closes shut; the mouth is a round plated ring facing DOWN, not a mouth on the front of the face. First round (2026-07-31) drew a lobster with pincer claws and a jawed mouth — exactly what this negative forbids. Redo needed with this stronger wording.

arrivals.name: Plants reach land
arrivals.line: Spores, nothing you could call a plant yet. Land has been bare for four billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a cluster of four spores fused into one tetrahedral group — a cryptospore tetrad — each spore a small rounded ball with a finely pebbled surface, the four packed together like soap bubbles
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf, not a stem and not moss: at this date there is nothing anyone would call a plant, only spores. Not a single sphere — the diagnostic is the bonded group of four. Keep them warm translucent amber, never near-black.
arrivals.reference: Rubinstein et al. 2010, *New Phytol.* — Ordovician cryptospore tetrads

arrivals.name: The Late Ordovician extinction
arrivals.line: Ice, then anoxia. About 85% of species go.
arrivals.analogy: several graptolite fossils fanning out from one point on a pale grey shale slab — each a narrow straight strip edged with fine regular teeth, like the blade of a hacksaw flattened into the rock
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a fern frond and not a feather: graptolites are straight or gently curved toothed strips preserved as a flattened film. The film must read as a mid-tone silvery grey against a lighter slab, never black, or the luminance key punches it out of the artwork.
arrivals.reference: *Dicellograptus* and *Climacograptus* specimen photographs; Harper et al. 2014

arrivals.name: *Cooksonia*
arrivals.line: The first plants with stems. A few centimetres tall, and the tallest thing alive.
arrivals.analogy: a few centimetres of forking, leafless green stems, splitting into two even branches again and again, with small rounded capsules at the branch tips
arrivals.negative: not a plant with leaves or roots — bare forking stems only, nothing frond-like or leafy

arrivals.name: *Tiktaalik*
arrivals.line: A fish with a neck, and wrists.
arrivals.analogy: a coelacanth lying flat and horizontal, as if resting on a stream bed: the same heavy scales, the same three-lobed tail, and a pair of thick, fleshy-based front fins ending in a fan of stiff fin-rays — but with a much flatter, much wider head, almost crocodile-flat, and both eyes set on top of it, looking straight up
arrivals.negative: not standing, not walking, not upright on four legs, and not a salamander, newt, lizard, amphibian or frog. The whole animal lies flat and horizontal in the water, exactly like the coelacanth it is drawn from — the head is the one place it departs from an ordinary coelacanth, wider and flatter, with the eyes on the very top looking up rather than out to the sides. Every fin ends in a smooth unbroken fan of fin-rays — no toes, no fingers, no claws, nothing hand-shaped or foot-shaped anywhere on the animal. Four rounds (2026-07-31) each held one half of the animal and lost the other: an upright walking version with no fish left in it, then a fish missing the join between head and shoulders, then that join back but with toed feet, then a fully standing frog. Naming the tetrapod parts it must not have made it worse each round. Round five (2026-08-01), coelacanth-anchored and clear of neck/wrist/propped/limb: failed a third way — a small round-bodied orange reef fish, side-set eyes, no flattening to the head at all, nothing coelacanth-shaped beyond a vaguely lobed fin. Naming the coelacanth was not enough; the head's actual shape needs a second, independent anchor next round — e.g. a hammerhead shark's flattened head-plane, or a duck-billed platypus's flat broad snout, held next to the coelacanth's body and tail so the departure is anchored on both ends instead of asserted once.
arrivals.reference: Tiktaalik roseae holotype photographs and reconstructions — Daeschler et al. 2006, *Nature*; Field Museum; coelacanth (*Latimeria*) reference photographs, NOAA Fisheries / Smithsonian Ocean

arrivals.name: The coal forests
arrivals.line: Trees 40 metres tall, in swamps that become every coal seam on Earth. The air is 30% oxygen and the dragonflies are 70 cm across.
arrivals.analogy: a giant dragonfly, long segmented body, two pairs of long net-veined wings held flat to the sides
arrivals.negative: not modern dragonfly proportions — enormous, wingspan wider than a hawk's, same basic wing shape

arrivals.name: *Dimetrodon*
arrivals.line: Not a dinosaur. A synapsid — our own branch, 60 million years before the first dinosaur.
arrivals.analogy: a lizard-like animal with a tall sail of skin down its back, held up by long spines
arrivals.negative: not a dinosaur — it walks with a sprawling reptile-like gait, and it predates dinosaurs entirely

arrivals.name: The Great Dying
arrivals.line: Siberian basalt cooks the ocean. 81% of marine species die, in about 60,000 years — one and a half pixels.
arrivals.analogy: a thick slab of flood-basalt crust broken open, its top a ropy wrinkled skin like cooled porridge, with a narrow orange glow showing only in the deep cracks between the crusted plates
arrivals.negative: not a volcano with a cone, not an eruption scene and not a landscape — the Siberian Traps were floods of lava across flat ground, not a mountain. One slab. The crust stays a mid-toned grey-brown, never near-black, and the glow is confined to narrow cracks.
arrivals.reference: pāhoehoe basalt crust photographs; Siberian Traps flood basalt specimens; Burgess et al. 2014, *PNAS*

arrivals.name: The first dinosaurs, and the first mammals
arrivals.line: Both lines appear inside the same eight million years. At this scale, the same moment.
arrivals.analogy: two small animals side by side at the same scale, overlapping slightly so they read as one group: a slender bipedal dinosaur on long hind legs with its tail held level behind it, and beside it a shrew-sized furry mammal on four legs with a long pointed snout
arrivals.negative: not a large dinosaur and not a modern mouse — both are small and early. The dinosaur is lightly built and bipedal, never a bulky quadruped, and its tail is held level and never drags. The mammal is furry with a pointed snout, not a round-eared rodent. Neither may be near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Eoraptor* and *Herrerasaurus* reconstructions (Ischigualasto); *Morganucodon* reconstructions

arrivals.name: The Triassic–Jurassic extinction
arrivals.line: The Atlantic starts to open. Half of everything dies, and the dinosaurs inherit it.
arrivals.analogy: a phytosaur — long and low like a gharial, with a long narrow tube-shaped snout full of small teeth, a raised volcano-like mound on top of the skull just in front of the eyes with the nostrils opening on top of it, four short legs and a long heavy tail
arrivals.negative: not a modern crocodile or alligator. The tip of the snout is solid and smooth with no nostril openings on it at all — the nostrils sit far back, up on a raised mound directly in front of the eyes. The snout is long, narrow and tube-like, not short and broad. The whole animal from snout tip to tail tip sits well inside its own quarter of the picture with clear empty space all around it. Two rounds (2026-07-31) drew a short-snouted crocodile with nostrils at the snout tip, then a tailless one that ran off the edge of its frame and baked cropped — redo needed.

arrivals.name: *Archaeopteryx*
arrivals.line: Feathers, and the first wing that works.
arrivals.analogy: a raven-sized dinosaur-like animal with sharp teeth, a long bony tail, and feathered wings
arrivals.negative: not a modern bird — teeth and a long bony tail, not a beak and a fan of tail feathers

arrivals.name: The first flowers
arrivals.line: *Archaefructus*: no petals yet, but a flower — the oldest anyone can date. Before this, nothing was in bloom.
arrivals.analogy: a slender aquatic stem with finely divided feathery leaves, carrying along its upper length a row of small paired seed pods and bare stamens attached directly to the stem, with no petals anywhere
arrivals.negative: not a modern flower: no petals, no sepals, no bloom and no blossom shape of any kind. *Archaefructus* is a thin water plant whose reproductive parts sit bare along the stem. Not a lily, not a magnolia, not a daisy. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Sun et al. 2002, *Science* — *Archaefructus sinensis* holotype

arrivals.name: *Tyrannosaurus rex*
arrivals.line: The last and largest of the tyrannosaurs, gone within two million years of the asteroid.
arrivals.source: Fowler 2017, *PLOS ONE* — Hell Creek Fm. and equivalents, 68–66 Ma
arrivals.analogy: a huge two-legged predator held horizontal like a see-saw balanced over its hips — spine level, a long heavy tail carried straight out behind as a counterweight, a short deep S-curved neck, and an enormous blunt boxy head of thick conical teeth; tiny forelimbs held to the chest with exactly two clawed fingers, and thick bird-like hind legs with three forward-facing toes
arrivals.negative: not upright like a kangaroo, and the tail never drags on the ground — that reconstruction is a century out of date. Exactly two fingers on each hand, not three. No fur and no coat of feathers. Not green, not a lizard and not roaring. Keep it light-to-mid in value throughout.
arrivals.reference: *Tyrannosaurus rex* skeletal mounts AMNH 5027 and FMNH PR2081; modern horizontal-posture reconstructions

arrivals.name: Chicxulub
arrivals.line: Everything larger than a badger dies.
arrivals.analogy: the whole Earth as a disc, most of it under heavy swirling white and grey-brown storm cloud and dust, one brilliant white-hot flash and an expanding pale ring spreading from a single point, with only broken fragments of green land and blue ocean showing through the gaps
arrivals.negative: not a clean blue-and-green globe with recognisable continents — cloud and dust cover most of the disc and the coastlines are broken up and mostly hidden, so no continent is identifiable and no modern shape can be read off it. No night side, no crescent, no dark limb, and nothing anywhere on the disc may be black or near-black. Three rounds (2026-07-31) drew the modern world whenever the palaeogeography was prompted explicitly, however forcefully it was forbidden, so the geography is now veiled by the event itself rather than drawn — which is what the other three planet portraits already do (§11).

arrivals.name: The first true primates
arrivals.line: *Teilhardina* — not the primate-like mammals that came before it, but the first crown primate. It appears on three continents within 25,000 years, during a sudden burst of global heat.
arrivals.source: Smith, Rose & Gingerich 2006, *PNAS* — Teilhardina, PETM onset ~56 Ma
arrivals.analogy: a small squirrel-sized animal gripping a branch, its hands and feet wrapped right around it, with large forward-facing eyes, short soft fur and a long slender tail held out for balance
arrivals.negative: not a monkey and not a ring-tailed lemur: an early primate is small, generalised and squirrel-like. Not a rodent either — the giveaway is grasping hands with real fingers curled round the branch, and eyes facing forward rather than out to the sides. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Teilhardina* and *Carpolestes* reconstructions; Bloch & Boyer 2002, *Science*

arrivals.name: Antarctica freezes
arrivals.line: The greenhouse world ends. The modern icehouse begins.
arrivals.analogy: a slab of ice calving off a dark rock cliff into the sea
arrivals.negative: not a whole ice-covered planet like Snowball Earth — one coastal cliff, one iceberg

arrivals.name: The human line splits from the chimpanzees
arrivals.line: Everything you would call human happens after this point — the next 175 pixels.
arrivals.analogy: a single ape skull in three-quarter view: a low rounded braincase, a heavy continuous brow ridge above the eyes, a short flat face and a broad palate of small worn teeth
arrivals.negative: not a modern human skull with a high domed forehead, and not a modern chimpanzee — this is the common ancestor's grade, so the braincase stays low and the brow heavy. No flesh, no hair and no ape-man portrait. The eye sockets must be shallow mid-toned recesses, never near-black, or the luminance key punches holes straight through the skull.
arrivals.reference: *Sahelanthropus tchadensis* cranium TM 266-01-060-1; Brunet et al. 2002, *Nature*

withheldNote: Held back from the scroll entirely, delivered in the finale fan. Label + date only. No line, no art, ever. Fan rows keep the point date (§8) — which is why `Fire, kept` shows `~800 ka` rather than the card notation `≥ 800 ka` it would carry if it had a card.
fieldNote: The field keyframes (spec §6). Colour is a DATA CHANNEL: the background is the era's actual
sky and ocean colour, so it is a scientific claim and cannot drift into a decorative rainbow.
Every transition takes its TRUE duration in pixels — no arbitrary easing, no announced cuts —
so the drift RATE is itself a data channel. Pixel positions are derived from `ma`, never stored.
`origin` records where each value came from: `prototype` = the cadence prototype's measured table;
`spec` = forced by a §6 rider; `approved` = authored here from §6's words and signed off by Dustin 2026-07-31.

copy.closing: The last ten happened in the final 110 of 115,000 pixels. Everything humans have farmed, written, built or remembered is the last three tenths of one pixel.
